title: Staged Traffic Marshal: declarative policy engine for progressive model rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a declarative rollout and policy engine (Staged Traffic Marshal) that encodes traffic splits, step schedules, shadow traffic, A/B experiments, and automatic rollback guardrails. The engine should be pluggable into Redwood routing and support pinned model versions, rollout histories, and audit logging. Goals: 1) Enable safe progressive releases with explicit step definitions and adaptive waits, 2) Provide guardrails driven by SLOs and quality signals (latency, error rate, hallucination regression on eval prompts), 3) Support shadow traffic mirroring and multi-variant A/B traffic splits, 4) Integrate with Console for visualization and manual overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Policy objects can be authored as YAML/JSON and applied via the rollout API
Runtime enforces traffic splits at router with <1% added latency in steady state
Guardrail rules trigger automated rollback within configured cooldowns when thresholds breached
Shadow traffic mirror mode forwards 10-100% of production traffic to candidate without affecting latency to users
Console shows per-step metrics (request count, p50/p95 latency, error rate, eval-quality delta) and a clear rollback button
All rollout events are recorded in audit log with who/when/why and associated model_version
implementation_plan: Design policy schema (steps, conditions, transitions) and DSL for simple expressions
Prototype runtime evaluator in the router that consumes policy and exposes a read-only ``current_state`` endpoint
Add guardrail adapters for core metrics: latency p95, error rate, token cost, custom eval pass-rate
Implement shadow mirroring path with configurable sampling and response discard semantics
Console integration: renderer for policy steps, timeline visualization, manual step advance/rollback
End-to-end tests and staged rollout on canary tenant before org-wide rollout
design_decisions: Persist policies in ConfigService as versioned objects to enable rollbacks and auditability
DSL will be intentionally small: comparisons, sliding-window aggregations, and boolean composition; avoid Turing-complete expressions to keep evaluation predictable
Make guardrail thresholds configurable per-release with sensible org defaults (e.g., p95 < 250ms for low-latency models, error_rate < 0.5%)
Reactive waits: policy can express a minimum observation window (e.g., 15m) and adaptive extension if metric variance is high
Do not embed heavy ML evaluation in the critical path; quality regressions are based on batched offline evals reported as signals to the policy engine
tradeoffs: Storing policies centrally improves observability and audit but adds config-service availability dependency
Simple DSL reduces expressivity but improves safety and makes static analysis for auto-rollback easier
Running eval-quality signals async reduces user impact but introduces delay in rollback reaction to hallucinations
Making shadow traffic synchronous would give better quality signals but risks production latency; we choose asynchronous mirroring for safety
progress_updates: 2025-02-03: Kickoff meeting with Eng, PM, and Console design. Agreed on minimal policy schema and key guardrail metrics.
2025-02-07: PoC: router can apply fixed traffic split for two variants using staged-marshal prototype (internal branch: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/452).
2025-02-10: Design review completed. UX wireframes for Console timeline and manual controls uploaded to Confluence (confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Staged+Traffic+Marshal).
2025-02-12: Implemented guardrail adapter for p95 latency and error rate. Unit tests added. Integration tests failing intermittently under load—investigating race in metrics aggregation.
2025-02-14: Code review feedback left on PR #478: ensure policy parsing failures are fail-safe (reject apply), add schema migration tests, and add RBAC checks for rollout creation.
tests: E2E: apply policy with three steps (1%, 10%, 50%) and validate step transitions under healthy metrics
Failure injection: cause p95 spike and confirm auto-rollback triggers and audit event emitted
Shadow path: mirror 20% of traffic and assert mirrored responses do not affect production latencies
A/B experiment: run two variants with 40/60 split and validate metric attribution in Console
Chaos test: simulate ConfigService downtime and ensure router rejects policy changes but continues serving current policies
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy metrics can cause flapping between steps. Mitigation: implement hysteresis with minimum observe windows and require consecutive violating windows before rollback.
Risk: policy parsing errors could block deployments. Mitigation: dry-run validation API and schema linter in CI.
Risk: unauthorized rollout creation. Mitigation: enforce RBAC and require explicit approval for production scopes.
Risk: data privacy for mirrored traffic. Mitigation: redact PII in mirrored payloads and only mirror to dedicated non-production clusters with KMS-backed keys.
notes: Ask: PM to coordinate with Solutions for initial canary tenant selection and SRE for alerting thresholds.
Follow-up: add data retention policy for mirrored traffic logs; align with legal on PII redaction.
Next: complete schema migrations and address flaky integration test by Feb 20th.
